definition.def: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.
examples: An intense debate is going on within the Israeli government.
There has been a lot of debate among scholars about this. [+ about]

definition.def: A debate is a formal discussion, for example in a parliament or institution, in which people express different opinions about a particular subject and then vote on it.
examples: There are expected to be some heated debates in parliament over the next few days.

definition.def: If people debate a topic, they discuss it fairly formally, putting forward different views. You can also say that one person debates a topic with another person.
examples: The United Nations Security Council will debate the issue today. [VERB noun]
The causes of anorexia are much debated. [pl-n V n]
Scholars have debated whether or not Yagenta became a convert. [VERB wh]
He likes to debate issues with his friends. [VERB noun + with]

definition.def: If you debate whether to do something or what to do, you think or talk about possible courses of action before deciding exactly what you are going to do.
examples: Taggart debated whether to have yet another coffee. [VERB wh]
At the moment we are debating what furniture to buy for the house. [VERB wh]
I debated going back inside, but decided against it. [VERB verb-ing]

definition.def: If you say that a matter is open to debate, you mean that people have different opinions about it, or it has not yet been firmly decided.
examples: Which of them has more musical talent is open to debate.
